 Jax State Student Workers and Union Advocates Call for $10 Minimum Hourly Wage
 November 7, 2026 
 Lee Evancho 
 JACKSONVILLE, AL — United Campus Workers–Jax State (UCW-Jax State) and Friends of the Union–Jax State (FOTU) are calling on Jacksonville State University to increase its minimum student worker wage to $10 per hour, citing concerns about compensation, student retention and the rising cost of living.
 The organizations announced their proposal following the university Board of Trustees’ recent approval of a 2% cost-of-living adjustment for employees. While acknowledging the increase as a positive development, union representatives expressed concern that student workers, adjunct and visiting faculty, and other part-time employees were excluded from the adjustment.
 According to UCW-Jax State, many student employees currently earn $8.25 per hour. The organization reported that its review of comparable institutions found advertised student wages ranging from $10 to $15 per hour.
 UCW-Jax State and FOTU have formally requested that university leadership establish a $10 minimum hourly wage for student employees. A certified letter outlining the proposal and supporting research has been sent to university administrators for consideration.
 The organizations described the proposed increase as an initial step toward a broader goal of establishing a $15 minimum hourly wage for all campus workers.
 Union representatives also connected the proposed wage increase to student retention and academic success, referencing Alabama’s recently enacted CHEER Act and its emphasis on improving educational outcomes.
 According to the organizations, the initiative is being led primarily by Jax State students, including student workers who have expressed concerns about balancing employment responsibilities with their academic commitments.
 The groups stated that higher wages could allow some students, particularly first-generation college students, to reduce the number of jobs they hold or pursue employment opportunities on campus rather than commuting to off-campus positions.
 Advocates maintain that increasing student wages could help reduce financial pressures and provide students with additional time to focus on their education.
 UCW-Jax State, affiliated with Communications Workers of America Local 3821, represents campus workers advocating for compensation and workplace improvements. Friends of the Union–Jax State is a student organization that works alongside the union on issues affecting students and university employees.
 The organizations thanked university leadership for considering the proposal and indicated they intend to continue advocating for incremental wage increases.
